Thanks for flagging — quick technical clarity: the calendar event was created with the label "Central European Time" in our scheduling flow but the underlying event timestamp was stored in UTC. Because the US switched to DST on Mar 14, some clients (especially older Exchange connectors) are shifting the displayed hour.

To avoid ambiguity I’m proposing three concrete options (I listed them in UTC to be client-agnostic):

Option A — Tue Apr 2 13:00 UTC (14:00 CET / 09:00 ET) — preferred (keeps EU exec window and before Marissa’s travel)
Option B — Mon Apr 6 14:00 UTC (15:00 CET / 10:00 ET) — if Apr 2 doesn’t work
Option C — Keep Fri Apr 3 but change explicit invite timezone to "Europe/Paris (CET)" and add UTC time in the description (risk: Marissa unavailable)

I can update the Google Calendar invite using an explicit IANA timezone (Europe/Paris) and add the UTC timestamp in the event description. That usually prevents Outlook/Exchange connectors from flipping the hour.

Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — Option A (Tue Apr 2 13:00 UTC / 14:00 CET / 09:00 ET) works best for our schedule and keeps our UK execs happy. Please send an updated invite with the explicit "Europe/Paris (CET)" timezone and the UTC timestamp in the body; that will prevent our scheduler from shifting it.
